2609.03355.title: ALRA: Adaptive Local Relational Alignment for Logit-Based Pre-training Distillation of Autoregressive Language Models
2609.03355.paper_summary: Logit-based knowledge distillation for autoregressive language models usually aligns teacher and student next-token distributions over the entire vocabulary. However, this global objective overlooks relative preferences among likely token alternatives. Existing local approaches often select candidate tokens from either the teacher or the student alone. Teacher-only selection can miss tokens that the student considers likely, while student-only selection can rely on an inaccurate ranking early in training. We propose Adaptive Local Relational Alignment (ALRA), a position-specific framework combining student proposals with teacher guidance. At each valid prediction position, the student proposes likely tokens, while the teacher's most probable token is included as an anchor. ALRA adjusts the number of selected tokens according to how broadly the teacher distributes probability within this candidate set relative to the current batch. Adaptive Local Divergence retains the mass-matching term and separately matches the relative token distributions within the selected and remaining vocabulary regions. Unlike the exact full-vocabulary decomposition, it replaces the teacher-mass coefficients of the two conditional terms with unit coefficients, preventing either term from being downweighted solely because its region has low teacher probability. Student-Weighted Pairwise Relational Alignment emphasizes high-probability token pairs with small student probability gaps and gives less weight to unlikely or clearly separated pairs. Experiments on The Pile with randomly initialized 200M- and 500M-parameter students across nine zero-shot benchmarks yield average accuracies of 36.62% and 37.40%. ALRA exceeds the strongest competing distillation baseline by 0.94 and 0.83 percentage points and improves over pre-training without distillation by 2.31 and 2.91 points, respectively.
2609.03355.paper_summary_zh: Logit-based 知識蒸餾對於自回歸語言模型通常會對整個詞彙表的教師和學生下一個標記的分佈進行對齊。<lb/>然而，這個全局目標忽略了在可能的標記選擇之間的相對偏好。<lb/>現有的本地方法通常僅從教師或學生中選擇候選標記。<lb/>僅教師的選擇可能會錯過學生認為可能的標記，而僅學生的選擇可能依賴於訓練初期不準確的排名。<lb/>我們提出了自適應本地關係對齊（ALRA），這是一個位置特定的框架，將學生的提議與教師的指導結合起來。<lb/>在每個有效的預測位置，學生提出可能的標記，而教師的最可能標記則作為錨點包含在內。<lb/>ALRA 根據教師在這個候選集內相對於當前批次的概率分佈範圍調整選擇的標記數量。<lb/>自適應本地散度保留了質量匹配項，並分別匹配所選和剩餘詞彙區域內的相對標記分佈。<lb/>與精確的全詞彙分解不同，它用單位係數替換了兩個條件項的教師質量係數，防止任何一項因其區域的教師概率低而被降低權重。<lb/>學生加權成對關係對齊強調具有小學生概率差距的高概率標記對，並對不太可能或明顯分離的標記對給予較少的權重。<lb/>在 The Pile 上進行的實驗中，隨機初始化的 200M 和 500M 參數學生在九個零樣本基準上產生了平均準確率分別為 36.62% 和 37.40%。<lb/>ALRA 超過了最強競爭蒸餾基線 0.94 和 0.83 個百分點，並分別在沒有蒸餾的預訓練上提高了 2.31 和 2.91 個點。
